dimensions.reasons: The submitted scene is recognizably a retro-industrial machine mounted on a long workbench. Group B frames visibly progress from an unobstructed mechanism in frame_0001 to a large extruded brass title reading “MOMENTUM” in frame_0200, so the requested kinetic-typography concept is substantially present.
issues: The key teaching focus—the mechanically legible drive chain—is not clearly readable in the finished views.
The requested pair of three-joint pick-and-place arms, paired camshafts, and an evidently meshed multi-gear train cannot be confidently identified.
The final title letters obscure much of the apparatus rather than leaving its layers clearly separable.

dimensions.reasons: The workbench has a substantial layered top, lower braces, and legs that visibly reach the floor in Group B frame_0001. The completed letters appear aligned on the front rail/bench surface, and the right flywheel assembly is broadly mounted to a base.
issues: The central red arm and stacked pale assembly have unclear structural support, especially in the dark Group A views.
The long far-right diagonal rod appears unattached or ambiguously connected in cam_submitted and the wide evaluator views.
Many pivots, rods, and gear-to-shaft connections are hidden by darkness, making the mechanism's functional continuity difficult to verify.

dimensions.reasons: The bold extruded letters are clearly letterforms rather than boxes, and Group B frame_0200 makes the full MOMENTUM title readable. Brass/gold rails, a gold flywheel, dark steel-like supports, reddish mechanical members, and a dark wooden bench establish the requested retro-industrial visual language.
issues: Most brass reads as clean, highly reflective gold rather than visibly worn or lightly oxidized brass.
Steel components are too shadowed to consistently read as cool-grey clear-coated metal.
Extreme black clipping and highlight glare remove the intended identity of several smaller mechanical parts.

dimensions.reasons: The author renders have a deliberate cinematic workshop mood, with reflections on the floor, directional highlights, and a coherent dark-room setting. The bench and the better-lit flywheel/letter surfaces retain some material depth.
issues: Group B frames are severely underexposed over much of the apparatus, while multiple background lights are blown out into large white bloom blobs.
Strong contrast crushes mechanical detail and makes the image unsuitable as a clear step-by-step demonstration.
Motion blur heavily smears the central arm/rod area in early animated imagery rather than clarifying motion.

dimensions.reasons: The broad layout follows the intended horizontal factory-machine arrangement: a long bench and rails span the image, letter assembly occurs along the front, and the most visible wheel/gear cluster sits at the right. The title is evenly organized into a single row by Group B frame_0200.
issues: The conveyor route, camshaft locations, and handoff path between the supposed robotic arms are not visually legible.
The overhead brass beam and final letter row obstruct the mechanisms that students are supposed to distinguish.
The spatial relationship of the red arm, pale vertical supports, and the diagonal right rod is unclear in several angles.

dimensions.reasons: The large title spans the workbench convincingly, the wheel cluster is appropriately smaller than the bench length, and the overall bench-to-machine relationship reads as a plausible display-scale industrial installation.
issues: The tall vertical and diagonal rods extend far above or beyond the compact mechanism and look disproportionately isolated.
Because much of the mechanism is lost in darkness, the specified relative sizes of the 400 mm main gear and 60–200 mm driven gears cannot be verified.
The visual scale relationship between the letters, conveyor, and robotic arm elements is not consistently clear.

dimensions.reasons: A warm brass-oriented key look and cool bluish floor/rim reflections are visible in the author renders, particularly Group B frames 0001 and 0200. The gold title and flywheel have convincing specular response, while the bench retains a dark wood-like surface.
issues: The lighting is excessively contrasty for the requested instructional clarity.
Specular clipping and bloom conceal surface wear, bevel detail, rivets, and material distinctions.
Ambient fill is insufficient: many metal and wood surfaces collapse into nearly featureless black.

dimensions.reasons: The workbench, rails, industrial decorative details, multiple visible wheel/gear forms, large extruded letters, and a completed MOMENTUM word are present. Group B frame progression also provides evidence of a PNG-sequence-style letter buildup.
issues: Only one red arm-like assembly is clearly visible; two distinct three-joint robotic arms are not demonstrated.
Two identifiable camshafts with reciprocating push rods and a clearly readable 2 m conveyor are not visible.
A same-module train with the specified main gear plus several visibly meshing driven gears is not verifiable from the renders.

The time-ordered Group C frames appear effectively unchanged from frame_0001 through frame_0016, so the submitted animation-video evidence does not visibly show the letter-assembly sequence seen in the Group B PNG frames.

criteria.criterion: The complete machine choreography must assemble and lock MOMENTUM through a synchronized, unobstructed, pedagogically readable sequence.
The complete gear train must satisfy the stated dimensions, common-module compatibility, connected engagement, and mechanically compatible operation.
Two identifiable camshafts must each produce recurring push-rod reciprocation.
The conveyor must have the stated transport length and visibly feed letter blanks into the handling workflow.
Two three-joint robotic arms must both perform letter pick-and-place.
All eight title letters must share the specified bold sans-serif form and dimensions.
The supporting bench must satisfy its dimensions, base role, construction detailing, and complete dark matte wood finish.
The machine must achieve the requested retro-industrial kinetic-typography identity through a coherent old mechanism and its complete brass-and-steel surface system.
criteria.evidence: The exported final frames clearly show a brass/gold mechanical bench with gears, rails, and large metallic typography, plus some bright silver-grey components. However, the brass appears predominantly clean, highly polished gold under extreme bloom rather than visibly worn or lightly oxidized, and the crushed blacks/glare prevent a clear, coherent read of a complete brass-versus-cool-grey-steel surface system.

criteria.criterion: The native lighting setup and authored result must jointly provide the requested warm key, cool rim, ambient fill, and interior HDRI.
The authored shot must use the requested ordered movement, focal length, and readable shallow-focus treatment.
The delivered Blender project must be openable, editable, complete, and preserve the requested native Cycles rendering configuration and motion-blur result.
The actual PNG sequence and composited MP4 must form a complete, openable output package with the required resolution and timing.

notes: The submission successfully establishes a recognizable brass-and-steel kinetic-typography machine and ultimately shows a readable MOMENTUM title. Its central failure is clarity: extreme darkness, glare, occlusion, and ambiguous mechanical connections prevent the drive chain and requested arm/cam/conveyor system from functioning as a clear, teachable linkage demonstration.
score_policy: Frozen paper score: uncapped 0.5 rubric + 0.5 dimension.
